findings.claim: In July 2010, more than fifteen years ago, Michael Dell agreed to pay a personal $4 million penalty and to a permanent injunction to settle SEC charges over disclosures that hid how much Intel payments drove Dell's earnings; Dell Inc. paid $100 million. Both settled without admitting or denying the charges, and no later change to this outcome was found.

In November 2022 Dell Technologies agreed to pay $1 billion in cash to settle a Delaware suit alleging that controlling shareholders, including Michael Dell and Silver Lake, shortchanged Class V holders in a 2018 share swap; plaintiffs had sought $10.7 billion. No admission was reported, and in August 2024 the Delaware Supreme Court affirmed the $266.7 million legal fee award.

In December 2017 the Delaware Supreme Court reversed a 2016 Chancery appraisal that had valued Dell shares at $17.62, about 28% above the $13.75 paid in the 2013 buyout led by Michael Dell and Silver Lake. It was a valuation case: no finding of wrongdoing was made, and the court called the sale process sound.

In August 2023 Australia's Federal Court ordered Dell Australia, a Dell Technologies subsidiary, to pay a A$10 million penalty after it admitted overstating discounts on more than 5,300 add-on monitors sold on its website; it was also ordered to refund affected customers.

findings.entity: Dell Inc. and Dell Financial Services
findings.claim: In May 2008, over fifteen years ago, a New York State Supreme Court judge found in a suit by the state Attorney General that Dell used false and deceptive advertising of financing and warranty terms. Dell, which disputed the ruling, agreed in 2009 to pay $4 million in restitution, penalties and costs and to change its sales practices.

Five former employees filed a proposed class action against Dell Technologies in federal court in Texas in January 2026, alleging that it mismanaged its 401(k) plan with underperforming in-house target-date funds, at a claimed cost of over $318 million. These are allegations; no ruling was found.

Michael Dell was named in March 2026 to the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, where he had also served under President Bush. In December 2025 he and Susan Dell announced a gift to the new Trump Accounts programme at the White House with President Trump.

In May 2026 the Pentagon awarded Dell Federal Systems a five-year, $9.7 billion contract to supply Microsoft software, under three weeks after President Trump publicly urged Americans to buy a Dell. Officials said the award was competitive; ethics critics questioned the timing, and no finding of impropriety was reported.

In December 2025 Michael and Susan Dell pledged $6.25 billion to put $250 into Trump Accounts for about 25 million children. AL.com reported that the first deposits reached eligible children's accounts by 9 October 2026; the amount paid so far was not reported.

The Michael & Susan Dell Foundation's 2024 tax return reports $163.8 million in grants paid and $247.5 million in qualified charitable distributions, against assets worth about $7.8 billion at year end and $1.45 billion in contributions received that year.

Dell reports that its Scope 1 and market-based Scope 2 emissions fell from about 199,000 to 155,000 tonnes CO2e between fiscal 2023 and 2025, with limited third-party assurance. Its Scope 3 emissions, about 32.6 million tonnes in fiscal 2025, are over 200 times larger, and its 50% cut and 75% renewable electricity goals are for 2030.

ecology.reason: Dell Technologies makes computers, servers and storage, mostly through suppliers, so its footprint is indirect: electronics supply chains and the electricity its products use. It reports a cut of about a fifth in its own operational emissions between fiscal 2023 and 2025, but its value-chain emissions, about 32.6 million tonnes a year, are far larger. No major environmental incident was found.

politics.reason: Michael Dell sits on the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, as he did under President Bush, and announced his $6.25 billion Trump Accounts pledge at the White House with President Trump. Dell's unit won a $9.7 billion Pentagon software contract in 2026 weeks after the President praised the company; officials say it was competitive, and no political favour has been established.

social.reason: Dell's Australian arm paid a A$10 million court penalty in 2023 after admitting it overstated monitor discounts, and a New York court found in 2008 that Dell used deceptive financing and warranty advertising. Former employees allege in a pending 2026 suit that Dell mismanaged its 401(k) plan. Supplier working conditions were not checked beyond Dell's own audit figures.

legal.reason: Paid a personal $4 million penalty in 2010 to settle SEC charges that Dell hid large payments from Intel that let it meet earnings targets, without admitting or denying them. In 2022 Dell Technologies paid $1 billion to settle a suit naming him as a controlling shareholder over a 2018 share swap, without reported admission. Company matters include a 2023 Australian consumer penalty.

unresolved.reason: A proposed class action filed in 2026 alleges that Dell Technologies mismanaged its employees' 401(k) plan; it is pending at company level and no ruling has been made. No pending case naming Michael Dell personally was found. Questions raised about the timing of a 2026 Pentagon contract rest on reporting only.

proposal.counterweights: The Michael & Susan Dell Foundation paid $163.8 million in grants in 2024 ($247.5 million in qualifying distributions). The first $250 deposits from the Dells' $6.25 billion Trump Accounts pledge reached children's accounts in October 2026; the amount paid is not yet reported.
proposal.rationale: Legal stays 3 under R2 (personal SEC penalty); the 2010 matter is unchanged and the $1B Class V settlement, where he was a named defendant, is added. Social 1 to 2: a court-ordered consumer penalty and a court finding of deceptive practices are documented company-level problems. Unresolved 0 to 2: a pending company-level ERISA suit; none names him personally as far as found. Politics stays 1: an advisory seat and a public gift, no favour established. Ecology stays 1.
